title: Square root covariance update error and stability

items.title: An explicit rational envelope for the scaled Householder QR error
items.statement:
Let $q\ge n\ge1$, $u>0$, and let $\kappa_q$ be the local scaled-Householder
coefficient of [[lem-scaled-householder-step-meets-local-backward-error-premise]]
at active row dimension $q$. Set
$$\beta_{q,n}=(1+\kappa_q)^n-1,\qquad C_{q,n}=200qn.$$
If $C_{q,n}u<1$, then
$$\beta_{q,n}\le\eta_{q,n}:=\frac{C_{q,n}u}{1-C_{q,n}u}.$$
Thus the QR backward-error factor can be bounded by the stated rational
dimension-dependent expression in this precision range.

items.title: A factor perturbation gives an explicit Gram-matrix error
items.statement:
Let $G,E\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ and set $\widehat G=G+E$. Then
$$\|\widehat G\widehat G^T-GG^T\|_F \le 2\|G\|_F\|E\|_F+\|E\|_F^2.$$
The estimate is valid for all ranks, including $G=0$ and rank-deficient
factors.

items.title: The block QR measurement update gives the canonical Kalman update
items.statement:
Let $P^-=L^- (L^-)^T$ and $R=L_RL_R^T$, with real factors of arbitrary
rank. Let $H\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}$ and suppose
$$S=H P^-H^T+R\succ0.$$
Pad $L_R$ with zero columns so it has at least $p$ columns and form
$$Z=\begin{bmatrix}L_R^{\mathrm{pad}}&HL^-\\0&L^-\end{bmatrix}.$$
Take an exact reduced QR factorization $Z^T=UR$ with $U^TU=I$, set
$L=R^T$, and partition
$$L=\begin{bmatrix}L_{11}&0\\L_{21}&L_{22}\end{bmatrix}$$
at the observation and state dimensions. If needed, multiply each of the
first $p$ rows of $R$ by the sign of its diagonal entry, so that $L_{11}$ has
positive diagonal. Then
$$L_{11}L_{11}^T=S,\qquad L_{21}L_{11}^T=P^-H^T,$$
and
$$L_{22}L_{22}^T=P^- -P^-H^TS^{-1}HP^-.$$
For innovation $v=y-Hm^-$, the exact solve $L_{11}z=v$ gives
$m^-+L_{21}z=m^-+P^-H^TS^{-1}v$. Thus the factor update has exactly the
canonical one-step mean and covariance; $L_{22}$ may be singular.

items.title: QR prediction preserves the canonical covariance factor
items.statement: Let $P=LL^T$ with $L\in\mathbb R^{d\times r}$ and let $Q=L_Q L_Q^T$ with $L_Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times s}$, where zero columns and rank deficiency are allowed. For any real $F\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, form $G=[FL\;L_Q]$ and append zero columns if needed so that the transpose has at least $n$ rows. In exact arithmetic, if $G^T=UR$ is a reduced QR factorization with $U^TU=I$, then $L^-:=R^T$ satisfies $$ L^-(L^-)^T=FPF^T+Q. $$

items.title: Innovation, gain, and posterior errors follow from joint covariance perturbations
items.statement:
Let $S=S^T\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$ satisfy
$x^TSx\ge\mu\|x\|_2^2$ for all $x\in\mathbb R^p$, with $\mu>0$.
Let $B\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$, $D=D^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, and
let symmetric $E_S$ and matrices $E_B,E_D$ satisfy
$$\|E_S\|_F\le e_S<\mu,\qquad \|E_B\|_F\le e_B,\qquad \|E_D\|_F\le e_D.$$
Put $\widehat S=S+E_S$, $\widehat B=B+E_B$,
$\widehat D=D+E_D$, $\Phi=D-BS^{-1}B^T$, and
$\widehat\Phi=\widehat D-\widehat B\widehat S^{-1}\widehat B^T$.
If $b\ge\|B\|_2$, define $\beta=(\mu-e_S)^{-1}$. Then
$\widehat S\succeq(\mu-e_S)I\succ0$ and
$$\|\widehat S^{-1}\|_2\le\beta,\qquad \|\widehat S^{-1}-S^{-1}\|_2\le\mu^{-1}\beta e_S,$$
$$\|\widehat B\widehat S^{-1}-BS^{-1}\|_2 \le e_B\beta+b\mu^{-1}\beta e_S,$$
and
$$\|\widehat\Phi-\Phi\|_2 \le e_D+2b e_B\beta+b^2\mu^{-1}\beta e_S+e_B^2\beta.$$

items.title: An innovation solve residual gives a singular-value forward bound
items.statement:
Let $p\ge1$ and $T\in\mathbb R^{p	imes p}$ be nonsingular, define $$ \sigma_{\min}(T):=\min_{\|x\|_2=1}\|Tx\|_2, $$ and let $z_*=T^{-1}y$. For any computed vector $\widehat z$ with residual $r=T\widehat z-y$, $$ \|\widehat z-z_*\|_2\le rac{\|r\|_2}{\sigma_{\min}(T)}. $$ If $S=TT^T$ also satisfies $x^TSx\ge
u\|x\|_2^2$ for all $x$, with $
u>0$, then $\sigma_{\min}(T)\ge\sqrt
u$ and therefore $$ \|\widehat z-z_*\|_2\le rac{\|r\|_2}{\sqrt
u}. $$

items.title: Finite-horizon square-root Kalman filter by rectangular factors and QR
items.statement:
Fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$, positive state dimensions $d_k$ for
$0\le k\le T$, and positive observation dimensions $p_k$ for
$1\le k\le T$. Inputs are real finite matrices $F_k\in\mathbb R^{d_k\times
d_{k-1}}$, $H_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times d_k}$, observation vectors
$y_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k}$, and an initial mean $m_0\in\mathbb R^{d_0}$.
For each covariance supply a rectangular real factor
$$L_0\in\mathbb R^{d_0\times r_0},\qquad L_{Q,k}\in\mathbb R^{d_k\times r_{Q,k}},\qquad L_{R,k}\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times r_{R,k}},$$
where each column count is any finite nonnegative integer. The represented
covariances are $P_0=L_0L_0^T$, $Q_k=L_{Q,k}L_{Q,k}^T$, and
$R_k=L_{R,k}L_{R,k}^T$. Thus zero columns and rank-deficient factors are
allowed. The admissible statistical inputs are those of
[[def-linear-gaussian-state-space-model-with-independent-noises]] for which
the canonical innovation $S_k=H_kP_k^-H_k^T+R_k$ is positive definite at each
step. The [[def-axiom-of-choice]] assumption is inherited only for the
interpretation as a posterior; the finite matrix procedure itself uses no
probability-space choice.

Choose a unit roundoff $u$ in the no-underflow operationwise model of
[[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]].
Every matrix or vector product below is evaluated as left-to-right dot
products. A nonzero nonnormal intermediate, nonfinite result, zero innovation
diagonal, or failed factorization returns a status and the first failing step;
it is not coerced into a covariance
estimate. Each arithmetic and factorization failure has a declared return;
there is no iterative convergence loop or unbounded refinement search.

The QR operation used below is the following unpivoted reduced procedure on
$A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ with $m\ge n\ge1$. Initialize a working array
$R^{(0)}=A$ and an empty ordered reflector list. For $j=1,\ldots,n$, take
$x=R^{(j-1)}_{j:m,j}$ and $B=R^{(j-1)}_{j:m,j+1:n}$, call
[[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]] on $(x,B)$,
and, on success, replace the active block by its returned $C_+$. If the call
fails, return its first status and step. Store the exact orthogonal reflector
represented by the returned record, or the identity for its identity branch.
After $n$ successful steps, return the computed upper-triangular block
$R=R^{(n)}_{1:n,1:n}$ and the ordered reflector list representing the exact
product $Q_{\rm full}$ whose first $n$ columns are the reduced $Q$ factor.
Do not materialize a rounded dense $Q$. The conventions are those of
[[def-full-reduced-and-column-pivoted-computational-qr-factorisations]].

Initialize $m_{0|0}=m_0$ and $L_{0|0}=L_0$. At step $k$, perform the
following operations in order.

1. Compute the rounded mean prediction $\widehat m_{k|k-1}
=\operatorname{fl}(F_k\widehat m_{k-1|k-1})$. Form the rounded factor product
$\widehat X_k=\operatorname{fl}(F_kL_{k-1|k-1})$. Concatenate
$\widehat G_k=[\widehat X_k\;L_{Q,k}]$ and append zero columns until its
column count is $q_k=\max(d_k,r_{k-1|k-1}+r_{Q,k})$. Apply the above
reduced Householder QR procedure to
$\widehat G_k^T\in\mathbb R^{q_k\times d_k}$. On success let $R_k^{p}$ be
its reduced upper factor and set $L_{k|k-1}= (R_k^{p})^T$. No diagonal
positivity or full-rank condition is imposed on this prediction factor.

2. Compute $\widehat v_k=\operatorname{fl}
(y_k-\operatorname{fl}(H_k\widehat m_{k|k-1}))$. Pad $L_{R,k}$ with zero
columns to $\bar r_k=\max(p_k,r_{R,k})$ columns. Compute
$\widehat Y_k=\operatorname{fl}(H_kL_{k|k-1})$ and form the block prearray
$$\widehat Z_k= \begin{bmatrix} L_{R,k}^{\mathrm{pad}} & \widehat Y_k\\ 0 & L_{k|k-1} \end{bmatrix}.$$
Apply the above reduced Householder QR procedure to
$\widehat Z_k^T\in\mathbb R^{(\bar r_k+d_k)\times(p_k+d_k)}$. Its row
count is at least its column count. On success transpose its reduced upper
factor and partition the resulting lower factor as
$$\widehat L_k=\begin{bmatrix}\widehat L_{11,k}&0\\ \widehat L_{21,k}&\widehat L_{22,k}\end{bmatrix},$$
with block sizes $p_k$ and $d_k$. If any diagonal entry of $\widehat
L_{11,k}$ is zero, return `innovation-factorization-failure`. Otherwise,
multiply each row of the QR upper factor corresponding to that block by the
sign of its diagonal entry, an exact sign change, so that
$\widehat L_{11,k}$ has positive diagonal. This changes neither
$\widehat L_k\widehat L_k^T$ nor its lower block structure. No invertibility
or positive diagonal is required of $\widehat L_{22,k}$.

3. Solve $\widehat L_{11,k}\widehat z_k=\widehat v_k$ by forward
substitution in the order of
[[def-forward-and-back-substitution-for-triangular-systems]]. Set
$$\widehat m_{k|k}=\operatorname{fl} (\widehat m_{k|k-1}+\widehat L_{21,k}\widehat z_k),\qquad L_{k|k}=\widehat L_{22,k}.$$
Do not form a covariance downdate or an explicit matrix inverse. The
factor-defined covariance $L_{k|k}L_{k|k}^T$ is positive semidefinite as an
exact product of the returned entries; no claim is made that a separately
rounded materialization of that product remains positive semidefinite.

4. If any arithmetic operation or QR call returns a failure status, return the
first such failure and its step; if the leading innovation block has a zero
diagonal, return innovation-factorization-failure. Otherwise the finite loop
returns the predicted and updated mean/factor arrays with success. The success
status records arithmetic and factorization completion only.

For $T=0$ the loop is empty and the output is $(m_0,L_0)$ with no update
status. In exact arithmetic, the result implements the covariance and mean map of
[[alg-kalman-filter]]. The prediction factor identity is supplied by
[[lem-square-root-kalman-prediction-factor-identity]], and the measurement
block identity by
[[lem-square-root-kalman-measurement-block-factor-identity]]. Under the
inherited AC assumption
its statistical interpretation is the one in
[[thm-kalman-filter-is-exact-posterior]]. The nearby covariance supplied by
an unstructured QR backward error may introduce cross-correlations between
model blocks. Therefore no backward-stability claim within the original
independent-noise state-space model, and no uniform-in-time accuracy or
stability claim, is part of this procedure.

items.title: Product and Householder QR errors bound the represented joint covariance
items.statement:
Let $G\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}$, with $q\ge n$, be an exact prediction or
measurement prearray. Let $\widehat G$ be its computed version and assume
$$\|\widehat G-G\|_F\le e_{\mathrm{form}}+e_{\mathrm{in}},$$
where $e_{\mathrm{form}},e_{\mathrm{in}}\ge0$, $e_{\mathrm{form}}$ bounds
rounded products used to form the array, and $e_{\mathrm{in}}$ bounds
separately specified input-factor uncertainty. If
the successful scaled-Householder QR of $\widehat G^T\in\mathbb R^{q\times
n}$ has reduced upper factor $R$ and $L=R^T$, set
$$\kappa_q=\kappa_q(u),\qquad \beta_{q,n}=(1+\kappa_q)^n-1,\qquad \epsilon=e_{\mathrm{form}}+e_{\mathrm{in}}+ \beta_{q,n}\|\widehat G\|_F,$$
where $\kappa_q$ is the explicit local coefficient in
[[lem-scaled-householder-step-meets-local-backward-error-premise]]. Then
$$\|LL^T-GG^T\|_F\le2\|G\|_F\epsilon+\epsilon^2.$$
If $200qnu<1$, the rational envelope lemma
[[lem-square-root-kalman-householder-error-rational-envelope]] gives
$\beta_{q,n}\le\eta_{q,n}:=200qnu/(1-200qnu)$. In that regime the same
conclusion holds with
$\epsilon=e_{\mathrm{form}}+e_{\mathrm{in}}+\eta_{q,n}\|\widehat G\|_F$.
For one left-to-right rounded product $\widehat{UV}$ with inner dimension
$r$ and $ru<1$, a valid choice is
$e_{\mathrm{form}}=\gamma_r\|U\|_F\|V\|_F$; for several disjoint product
blocks, sum these bounds. This conclusion allows rank loss and does not imply
that the nearby joint covariance has the original independent-noise block
structure.

items.title: The square-root Kalman procedure returns a finite status
items.statement: For every finite admissible input to [[alg-finite-budget-square-root-kalman-filter]] with finite state and observation dimensions, the procedure returns after finitely many arithmetic operations. For $T>0$ its outcome is one of success, range-failure, or innovation-factorization-failure. This is a termination and status result only; it asserts neither that the numerical factorization succeeds nor that an error bound holds.

items.title: The square-root filter has an explicit conditioned finite-horizon error bound
items.statement:
Fix a finite horizon $T$ and let $(m_{k|k},P_{k|k})$ and
$(m_k^-,P_k^-)$ be the exact real-arithmetic prediction and update recursions
of [[alg-kalman-filter]]. Let
$$S_k=H_kP_k^-H_k^T+R_k,\qquad B_k=P_k^-H_k^T,\qquad v_k=y_k-H_km_k^-.$$
Suppose each innovation has a certified lower bound
$$x^TS_kx\ge\mu_k\|x\|_2^2\quad(x\in\mathbb R^{p_k}),\qquad \mu_k>0.$$
Let the procedure [[alg-finite-budget-square-root-kalman-filter]] output represented covariances
$\widehat P_{k|k}=\widehat L_{k|k}\widehat L_{k|k}^T$ and means
$\widehat m_{k|k}$. At step $k$, assume certified local bounds
$$\begin{aligned} &\|\widehat P_k^--(F_k\widehat P_{k-1|k-1}F_k^T+Q_k)\|_2\le e_k^P,\\ &\|\widehat J_k-J_k(\widehat P_k^-)\|_2\le e_k^J,\\ &\|\widehat m_k^--F_k\widehat m_{k-1|k-1}\|_2\le e_k^m,\\ &\|\widehat v_k-(y_k-H_k\widehat m_k^-)\|_2\le e_k^v,\\ &\|\widehat L_{11,k}\widehat z_k-\widehat v_k\|_2\le\rho_k,\\ &\|\widehat m_{k|k}-(\widehat m_k^-+\widehat L_{21,k}\widehat z_k)\|_2\le e_k^u, \end{aligned}$$
where
$$J_k(P)=\begin{bmatrix}H_kPH_k^T+R_k&H_kP\\PH_k^T&P\end{bmatrix}$$
and $\widehat J_k=\widehat L_k\widehat L_k^T$ is the joint covariance
represented by the measurement QR blocks. Let $f_k\ge\|F_k\|_2$,
$h_k\ge\|H_k\|_2$, $b_k\ge\|B_k\|_2$, and
$r_k\ge\|v_k\|_2$ be certified finite upper bounds. Choose
$\Delta_0\ge\|\widehat m_{0|0}-m_0\|_2+
\|\widehat P_{0|0}-P_0\|_2$.

Define recursively
$$c_k^H=1+h_k^2,\qquad \varepsilon_k=c_k^H(f_k^2\Delta_{k-1}+e_k^P)+e_k^J.$$
If $\varepsilon_k\le\mu_k/2$, put
$$K_k^\#=1+2b_k/\mu_k,\qquad C_k^K=\frac2{\mu_k}\left(1+\frac{b_k}{\mu_k}\right),\qquad C_k^P=2+\frac{4b_k}{\mu_k}+2\left(\frac{b_k}{\mu_k}\right)^2,$$
$$A_k=(1+h_kK_k^\#)f_k+ (C_k^Kr_k+C_k^P)c_k^Hf_k^2,$$
$$\eta_k=(1+h_kK_k^\#)e_k^m+ (C_k^Kr_k+C_k^P)(c_k^He_k^P+e_k^J)+ K_k^\#(e_k^v+\rho_k)+e_k^u, \qquad \Delta_k=A_k\Delta_{k-1}+\eta_k.$$
Then each $\widehat S_k$ is positive definite, the factor update is
defined, and, with $z_k^*=\widehat L_{11,k}^{-1}\widehat v_k$,
$$\|\widehat z_k-z_k^*\|_2\le \frac{\rho_k}{\sigma_{\min}(\widehat L_{11,k})} \le\sqrt{\frac2{\mu_k}}\,\rho_k,$$
where $\sigma_{\min}(T)=\min_{\|x\|_2=1}\|Tx\|_2$. Also
$$\|\widehat m_{T|T}-m_{T|T}\|_2+ \|\widehat P_{T|T}-P_{T|T}\|_2\le\Delta_T.$$
Equivalently,
$$\Delta_T=\left(\prod_{k=1}^T A_k\right)\Delta_0+ \sum_{j=1}^T\left(\prod_{k=j+1}^T A_k\right)\eta_j,$$
where an empty product is $1$. The bound is finite-horizon and explicitly
conditioned on the innovation margins and data scales. It implies no
uniform-in-time stability or accuracy claim.

title: Square root covariance update error and stability — Examples

items.title: A nonzero prearray perturbation changes the posterior but keeps its factor product PSD
items.statement:
Use a scalar state and observation with $P^-=R=H=1$. The exact measurement
prearray is
$$Z=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{bmatrix}.$$
For the perturbation calculation take
$$E=\begin{bmatrix}0&1/10\\0&0\end{bmatrix}, \qquad \widehat Z=Z+E.$$
This is a mathematical backward-perturbation example; it does not assert
that a particular floating-point QR produces this exact $E$.

items.title: A rounded subtractive covariance update can become indefinite
items.statement:
Use binary floating-point arithmetic with precision $p=24$, round-to-nearest
ties-to-even, and a normal exponent range containing the values below. Let
$$c=1-2^{-24},\qquad P^-=\begin{bmatrix}1&c\\c&1\end{bmatrix},\qquad H=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\end{bmatrix},\qquad R=2^{-22}.$$
Compute $B= P^-H^T$, then $S=HB+R$, then $K=B/S$, and finally
$P_{\rm sub}=P^- - (KS)K^T$, rounding every displayed operation in the
specified format.

items.title: A singular prior factor with a positive innovation remains admissible
items.statement: Take one state and one observation, one update step, $m_0=2$, $F=H=1$, $y=7$, and factors $L_0=L_Q=0$, $L_R=1$. The initial, process, and measurement covariances are $P_0=Q=0$ and $R=1$.

items.title: A nearly noiseless weakly scaled observation amplifies innovation-solve residual
items.statement: Take a scalar predicted variance $P^-=1$, observation coefficient $H=10^{-3}$, and measurement variance $R=10^{-12}$. For innovation $v=1$, suppose the computed triangular solve has residual $L_{11}\widehat z-v=10^{-9}$, with no other mean-update error.
